headers.//: THE HTML MUST NOT BE CACHED. Every script tag carries a ?v= so the JS files bust their own cache, but nothing busts the HTML that references them. A browser holding a cached portfolio.html therefore keeps requesting the OLD ?v= values, and any change to CSS or markup never lands at all. That produced a genuinely confusing failure: new JS behaviour appeared (short stage labels) while the CSS fix shipped in the same deploy did not, so the board still overlapped. must-revalidate means the browser asks every time and gets a 304 when nothing changed, which costs one round trip and removes a whole class of ghost bug.
Same for the bare paths, because cleanUrls serves /portfolio without the extension.
The versioned assets are the opposite case: their ?v= makes each URL unique, so they can be cached hard and a bump fetches a genuinely new URL.
